articleTitle: International Conference on Partial Discharge (Conf. Publ. No.378)
Time-resolved discharge measurements
abstract: This paper gives a short introduction in time-resolved discharge measurements and elucidates this detection method with the results obtained from measurements with 1 GHz bandwidth on polyethylene samples under prolonged discharge activity. It is shown that a correlation between the pulse shape and the physics of the discharge process is possible and that the start of severe degradation of the dielectric can be recognized in the shape of the discharge pulses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in partial discharge plant-monitoring technology
abstract: Partial discharge activity is both a symptom of degradation in the solid insulating systems of power plants-irrespective of the causative stresses-and a stress mechanism which causes degradation. It can therefore be readily appreciated why the detection, location and interpretation of pd activity is an attractive technique to the diagnostic engineer. Partial discharge (pd) activity can be detected by a variety of techniques, the most common being acoustical, optical, chemical and electrical techniques, and, in this brief overview, an attempt will be made to place these within the contest of individual items of plants. Also, the limitations of individual detection techniques will be discussed in the contest of power plant monitoring and some suggestions for future developments will be made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge signal generation, transmission and acquisition
abstract: Partial discharges (pd) play an important role in the ageing or breakdown scenario of solid, liquid and gaseous insulation systems. Their presence may indicate defects which reduce lifetime or reliability of an HV apparatus. If the partial discharge "signals" are correctly interpreted a risk evaluation may be done. Precondition for a correct interpretation of pd measurements are the understanding of the pd physics (i.e. physical models for the partial discharge process) and of the signal propagation (or transmission) in sometimes quite complex networks of HV apparatus plus the choice of a measurement procedure which is capable of predominantly revealing the partial discharge physics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge pattern recognition for three kinds of model electrodes with a neural network
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) signals have been studied for a long time as one of the significant high voltage test parameters and therefore many research works have been done on the sophistication of the PD measurement and data processing methods. PD characteristics can be derived from pulse data through statistical treatment of the data. With the aids of computer measurement systems, the phi -q-n distribution characteristics and the phi -q-n distribution characteristics have been proposed. Those characteristics add the voltage phase angle information to the conventional PD measurements. Recently, may applications of the phi -q-n distribution characteristics have been proposed. Those remarkable development in PD data processing may bring data-overflow in PD measurement. To treat a number of PD data requires the more sophisticated data processing method which fits the purpose of the high voltage tests. A neural network system was introduced to recognize the phi -q-n distribution pattern. This paper describes PD data processing as input signal for the neural network and the capability of the neural network system to recognize PD signals using four kinds of electrode systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pulse-sequence-analysis, a way to get a better insight into the physics of discharges
abstract: Partial discharge measurements are often used as a diagnostic tool to monitor degradation phenomena, whereby more or less sophisticated 'statistic packages' are used to evaluate the data sets. In contrast to the usual practice of considering only the statistic distributions of the data accumulated in a preset time interval, the paper proposes to use the direct pulse/pulse correlations of consecutive discharge pulses. Using data obtained in different stages of the growth of an electrical tree in polyethylene the advantages of the PSA-method are demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: From initiation to propagation in electric treeing
abstract: Our aim is to understand the electrical ageing of insulating polymeric materials in the absence of any pre-existing gaseous cavities in the bulk of the dielectric. We used a needle electrode moulded into the insulant with the aim to produce local field enhancement. The transition between the discharge-free to micro-partial discharge state (early electrical tree propagation phase) is investigated with a sensitivity reaching 0.01 pC. Correlation is made between length of tree and amplitude of discharges before any branching of the initial tree channel. The physics of discharge in such small volume is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A partial discharge monitor for the measurement of partial discharges in a high voltage plant by the transient earth voltage technique
abstract: Several proprietary discharge detectors are available that are suitable for measuring the magnitudes of the partial discharges in plants such as high voltage metalclad switchgear. Their main disadvantages are the high capital cost of the test equipment and the complexity of the testing procedure. When performing such tests, the plant must be switched out, connections must be made to the high voltage conductors of the plant under test and high voltages applied from a test set. A 'sanction for test' is therefore required. This overhead may be acceptable when testing primary or grid substations. However, for discharge measurements to be widely applicable it is essential that the tests can be made with the plant live and under load. The Transient Earth Voltage or TEV measurement technique has been developed to fulfil this requirement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Physical and chemical aspects of partial discharges and their effects on materials
abstract: Non-sparking discharges in gases at atmospheric pressure appear in the literature under different headings: non equilibrium plasmas, coronas, partial, silent and barrier discharges, electrical losses, ... But under these different names, which generally cover applications of different types, there exist common features with definite effects on insulating materials. This is the topic of the present introductive paper, which does not cover voids, of a micrometer range or less, where other physical mechanisms can enter into play.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detection of electrical tree initiation and assessment of shape of the developing tree using pattern recognition of partial discharge occurrence phase distribution
abstract: We have constructed a PD pulse measurement and degradation diagnosis system (PDM/ES-I) of materials suffering partial discharge using a personal computer. We applied PDM/ES-I to electrical tree degradation in low density polyethylene. The PD pattern measured at a given aging time was compared with five standard normalized PD patterns which had been registered in advance as five representative degradation stages. Consequently, the pattern recognition method proved to allow an exact determination of the time when the tree was initiated. In addition, the result of assessment agreed well with the observed tree shape.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of partial discharges on void gas pressure
abstract: The development of void gas pressure has been measured at different levels of voltage and thermal stress. The void gas pressure typically exhibits a fluctuating behaviour in the beginning of ageing and then subsequently decreases at a constant rate that increases for increasing voltage stress. It is larger at 50 degrees C than at room temperature. A characteristic pd-pattern was observed to develop after a certain ageing time dependent on the temperature level. The characteristic pd-pattern could to some extent be explained as an effect of indirect interaction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The physics of partial discharges
abstract: This paper will be restricted to pulsed partial discharges (PDs) associated with streamers in gases. For this class of discharges, a classification scheme and a generic approach for their physical modelling will be presented and it will be shown that such models allow one to derive relations between measured PD data, defect characteristics, and design and test parameters as important tools for PD interpretation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line PD analysis in power plants-a successful tool for early fault detection
abstract: Although partial discharge (PD) monitoring techniques are primarily applied for detecting internal discharges in polymer insulating materials, basically the same detection methods can also be used in a slightly modified form for online monitoring and for early fault detection in power plants. Faults in high-voltage equipment are often revealed by high-energy partial discharges or arcing. The resulting high-frequency pulses can be detected and analyzed by an online monitoring system. Such a system enables the sudden failure of vital equipment (generator, transformers) with severe consequential damage to be averted at an early stage. Thus improving the cost-effectiveness of the power plant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonstationary behavior of partial discharge during insulation aging
abstract: There are two purposes for this work. The first is to present an example of a case where a pulsating partial-discharge (PD) phenomenon exhibits non-stationary behavior associated with discharge-induced "aging" of a dielectric material. The observed nonstationary behavior, which manifests itself by a time-dependence in the statistical characteristics of PD pulses, illustrates the difficulties to be encountered in defining meaningful PD pulse "patterns" that can be used for reliable defect site identification. The second purpose is to point out possible difficulties in relating measured PD pulse-height distributions to measured average PD current which are relevant to the calibration of PD measurement systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phase-resolved partial discharge measurements and their electromagnetic spectrum in SF/sub 6/ gas
abstract: In this paper, we perform a fundamental study on partial discharge (PD) phenomena caused by creepage discharges in SF/sub 6/ gas. Besides phase-resolved PD pulse height measurements, electromagnetic spectra emitted from the PD are measured simultaneously. We also discuss the relation between PD statistical parameters and the spectra.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural network application in PD pattern analysis
abstract: The Computerised Discharge Analyser (CDA3) is a PC-based data acquisition system. It captures in real-time individual PD pulses from the output of a conventional analogue discharge detector. Integrated analysis of the raw data is carried out by software. It was shown that automatic recognition of the PD patterns is possible with the use of a neural network. The input to the network can be the bivariate phase-resolved distributions. Its size can be reduced by feeding the network with pre-processed data such as the statistical moments of the univariate distributions or the IEC-270 integrated quantities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On site very high frequency P.D. pulse measurements on full size rotating machine stator for discharge type recognition
abstract: The work described in this paper follows the study of the ageing kinetics of the insulating material submitted to P.D. in a test cell. The dependence of the natural frequencies of P.D. pulses on insulation age was found. Thus, a qualitative as well as quantitative new P.D. measuring apparatus could be developed for the monitoring of high-voltage rotating machine ageing. The P.D. measurements presented in this paper are part of the feasibility study of this new measuring device. Several measurements on real H.V. motors were needed to confirm the feasibility of a very high frequency P.D. pulse measuring device and recognition method. Very high frequency P.D. pulse measurements were performed on site on high voltage motor insulations, using the same type of instruments than those used previously in the laboratory on a motorette. The results published here show that, in full size insulations, the different types of P.D. pulses significant in different periods of ageing of the voids can be recognised by their frequency components. These results confirm the design of the P.D. measuring device built by SITELEC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discharges and the formation of tree-shaped breakdown structures
abstract: The picture of the electrical tree process that has emerged from a stochastic model is one of a discharging skeletal structure embedded within a space-charge region of its own creation. The space-charge controls the discharging pattern (spatially end temporally) and hence indirectly the discharge induced avalanche damage. Minor variations of the trapped space-charge density will lead to preferred directions for new channel formation, and provide a physical explanation for the random choice of the stochastic model. Regarding space-charge fields as contributing a negative feedback into the non-linear damaging process, treeing can be seen to be a consequence of a near-equilibrium situation. Conversely when the space-charge effect is small under a rapidly rising driving force, runaway in the form of a single puncture ensues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Directivity of acoustic signals from partial discharges in oil
abstract: For partial discharges in oil, the relationship between apparent discharge magnitude, electrically measured in pC, and the acoustic signal amplitude from the same discharge, shows large variations. If the acoustic signal is detected with several detectors simultaneously, it is found that the acoustic amplitudes are correlated in a relatively narrow angle range only. For larger angular separation, the acoustic amplitudes are uncorrelated and not anti-correlated. From this observation and some theoretical considerations, some physical aspects of streamers in oil are illuminated. The streamer velocity may, for example, be estimated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PD pulse distribution pattern analysis
abstract: Statistical data analysis has been recently requisite for partial discharge (PD) study. This has been enabled by the recent development of micro-processors or the downsizing of computers. It is important to pay much more attention for profiles of a packet of PD pulses to the voltage phase angle. Statistical parameters such as the skewness and the kurtosis have been intensively investigated for PD analysis. More recently, a neural network algorithm has been utilised especially to discriminate PD signals from noise signals for insulation diagnosis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach in PD diagnosis and PD pattern recognition
abstract: Digital measuring techniques and a few diagnosis systems have been developed to assist the test engineer. The most common diagnostic tools are two or three dimensional distributions or histograms which exhibit typical patterns of the PD activity. The main disadvantage of all these graphs in PD diagnosis is the integrative effect of the statistics used. In this paper the authors show a graph of Partial Discharge activity without any integrative effect that gains a diagnostic overview of the whole measurement. In this diagram the parameters charge, phase, time and test voltage are included, by this it is possible to summarize all significant information on one computer print. By seeing PD evolution from period to period, visual recognition and expert classification becomes practicable. Results of acoustical PD classification will be presented and the influence of test voltage on electrical and acoustical PD-recognition is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided partial discharge analyzing system for detection of swarming pulsive microdischarges
abstract: When diagnosing internal partial discharge (PD) degradation phenomenon, one must be cautions about swarming pulsive microdischarges (SPMD). However, the details of the main factors in the appearance of SPMD are not clear yet. One of the reasons is that there has been no way to measure SPMD quantitatively. Therefore we have developed a computer aided partial discharge analysing system (CAPDAS) which can evaluate SPMD, and introduced a new PD parameter, the SPMD ratio, for quantitative analysis of SPMD. It became clear that the enhanced appearance of initial electrons in internal voids promotes the change of normal PDs into SPMD.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New electrical method of identification of polymer ageing kinetics
abstract: We used a corona discharge test cell and an electronic device to measure the current under streamer impact to monitor on line the ageing of dielectric polymer foils. This method can also be used to identify different stages of polymer ageing and to characterise the electrical behaviour of aged samples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of partial discharges in condensed insulation
abstract: The aim of this report is to elucidate the relationship between the measurable partial discharge (pd) quantities and the characteristics of the void in which a partial discharge takes place. It is pointed out that the abc-equivalent is not a valid mathematical model of a pd. Mathematical expressions for the apparent and real charge are developed for spherical and disk-shaped cavities. It is shown that the apparent charge is proportional to the volume of the cavity and inversely proportional to the insulation thickness. It also depends upon the shape and site of the cavity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast image converter and slow computer simulation studies of partial discharge models
abstract: Partial discharges are particularly difficult animals to study in their natural habitat, as this invariably has been designed to exclude PDs and seldom to facilitate their observation. Even physical models are difficult to design to satisfy conflicting demands of observability and realism. The present paper discusses some results obtained by nanosecond electrical and optical measurements on a physical model of a PD void, and demonstrates the use of a simple circuit simulation program to interpret PD pulse measurements on a 50 Hz time scale.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with PD-measurements of stator windings
abstract: This paper reports on an off-line partial discharge (PD) detection system, taking the specific requirements of measurements of stator windings into account. A practical example demonstrates how PD-analyses can be used for condition assessment of stator winding insulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge measurements in underground distribution cable joints
abstract: The possibility of diagnosing properly electrical equipment, before an actual failure occurs in service, has always captivated utility personnel. In underground distribution, often work needs to be done in the proximity of live cables and accessories; these are in an unknown state of degradation and therefore, safety cannot be guaranteed to the workers. PD diagnosis was then the chosen approach to increase the level of confidence regarding work on underground cables and accessories. However, a decision threshold (under which no work should be allowed) remains to be established. This paper reports on a series of accelerated aging tests designed to find an actual value for this threshold; using a portable PD detector developed by our company, workers will be helped in making a decision whether or not to go ahead, by taking into consideration the suggested threshold values found in the lab.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A calibration procedure for computer controlled multichannel pulse-height analyzer
abstract: The availability of a Computer Controlled Multichannel Analyzer (MCA) Measurement System, for partial discharge (PD) measurements, opens interesting possibilities to develop software tools devoted to assist the calibration procedures. In this paper, a calibration routine designed to establish a correlation between the quantization level of the A/D converter and the apparent charge quantity in a complete test circuit, is presented and discussed. The proposed procedure is based on statistical processing of the calibration signals produced accordingly to IEC Std (1) or ASTM Std (2). In order to evaluate the correctness of the calibration results, some calibration factors are proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new technique for partial discharge testing high voltage polymeric cable in an open environment
abstract: In performing low-sensitivity, partial discharge (pd) testing in an open environment, several practical difficulties are experienced. The major obstacle encountered is the high ambient noise level resulting in an undesirable signal-to-noise ratio. The usual solution is to house all high-voltage test equipment and the cable under test in a shielded room to attenuate the noise sufficiently to perform the test. This paper describes new equipment that is capable of performing pd tests on cable in electrically noisy environments, without the benefit of a shielded room, resulting in savings in floor space and cost. The new shielded test systems are self-contained modules that combine all or some of the following components: power supply, high-voltage reactor, power separation filter (psf), high-voltage noise filter, and cable terminations, together with any necessary isolation transformer and power-line filters assembled and wired on a common pallet. The equipment can be configured for use with an existing power supply or as a complete system. Results of noise immunity tests on a complete system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge stressing of epoxy resin surfaces
abstract: An understanding of the degradation mechanisms of solid dielectrics under the action of partial discharge stressing, coupled to a characterisation of the various species and their prevalence under different conditions of stressing, will enable both the development of new insulating systems for power plants in the future and new diagnostic techniques to detect degradation in existing systems. This paper reports experimental work undertaken to study the changes brought about in an insulating resin formed from a diglyceride of bisphenol A cross-linked by phthalic anhydride, a common epoxy resin.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RFI measurements as a diagnostic technique for medium voltage transformers
abstract: The suitability of radio frequency interference (RFI) measurements for the detection and identification of internal discharges occurring in instrumentation and distribution transformers was studied in terms of detect sensitivity, interference tolerance and useability. Different types of medium voltage transformers having various faults were measured in a high voltage laboratory and at an open area test site.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge detection: theoretical and practical methods
abstract: The underlying principles of conventional partial discharge detection have been elucidated. These principles are shown to depend on the phenomenon of electricification by electrostatic induction. A discussion of this phenomenon enables the circuital aspects of partial discharge detection to be examined. It is concluded that, with reference to the determination of the maximum value of the induced charge, one should in normal test situations record the voltage transient rather than the current transient as this latter transient must be integrated to achieve the same result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical experience of partial discharge measurement and location on power cables
abstract: Unlike other items of plant installed in a High Voltage power network, the design limitations and dimensions on energy cables are effectively restricted by two dominant factors: conductor size and insulation thickness. These two factors have allowed and encouraged cable designers to operate insulation at the highest stress levels of any plant connected on the power system. To allow these high stress levels to be used reliably and ensure long service life, it is important to maintain a high standard of material and manufacturing quality during production. For this purpose, a partial discharge test has been a routine requirement for over 25 years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural networks as a tool for recognition of partial discharges
abstract: Three neural networks (NNs) were used to classify partial discharge (PD) patterns: 1. Back-propagation (BP) network with hyperbolic tangent transfer function and momentum term. 2. Kohonen self-organizing map (KOH) with conscience mechanism. 3. Extended version of learning vector quantization (LVQ) network with conscience mechanism. The results showed that all three types of NNs classified correctly test finger prints of trained PD patterns. Testing of the unknown and impossible finger prints resulted in a number of misclassifications. The important factor for obtaining satisfactory classifications was the choice of the correct number of neurons, learning cycles, and values of learning coefficients. Teaching times ranged from tens of seconds in the case of the BP network to some minutes in the case of the KOH and LVQ networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Risk functions for partial discharge inference in insulation systems
abstract: Partial discharges taking place in insulation systems may have different natures and locations. The identification of features which can be correlated to the partial discharge (PD) phenomena occurring in the system under test is a fundamental requirement for insulation diagnosis. The identification problem may be of difficult solution when more than one phenomenon are simultaneously occurring. In this paper, two-parameter Weibull distributions and multiplicatively-mixed Weibull distributions are used to infer data from PD measurements performed on specimens of stator bars laboratory-aged under accelerated procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discharge pattern recognition in high voltage equipment
abstract: For a long time recognition was performed by eye, studying PD patterns at the ellipse at an oscilloscope screen. In recent years the use of computer-aided processing provides automation of the recognition procedure. As a result, the partial discharge (PD) pulses are grouped by their phase-angle with respect to the sine wave. Consequently, the voltage cycle is divided into phase windows representing the phase angle axis 0-360 degrees . If the observation takes place for several voltage cycles, two- or three dimensional patterns can be observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Slot discharge mechanisms in high voltage rotating machines
abstract: High voltage stator winding insulation in modern rotating machines has a high degree of resistance to erosion by partial discharge but on-line monitoring of partial discharge activity can give useful early warning of physical degradation processes which could lead to premature insulation failure if not detected in time. Well defined changes in slot discharge pulse pattern have been shown to characterise the progression of physical damage due to movement of coil sides in the stator slots.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical discharges in liquids under direct voltage
abstract: In a non-uniform electrical field local discharges may occur at positions of high radius of curvature of the electrode surface without a full electrical breakdown resulting. Typically, as the direct field is raised progressively from a low value a situation may arise in which such small localized discharges can be recorded. The recording of a discharge may involve use of the shadow optical technique, or the discharge may be recorded as a current pulse through a resistor in series with the electrode system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling of partial discharges
abstract: We have developed multi-dimensional streamer models that can be applied to arbitrarily shaped electrodes. Our models have generated the first fully-resolved streamers which form self-consistent, multi-dimensional structures. The main objective of this paper is to demonstrate how the dynamical characteristics of streamers are determined by their multi-dimensional structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Acoustical method for partial discharge detection in high power capacitors
abstract: One of the most important aspects to be verified in the field is the presence of Partial Discharges (PD) inside the capacitors. A Partial Discharge activity in capacitors generates the emission of current pulses, which can be detected by electrical sensors or circuits, and acoustical waves, which can be detected by an acoustic sensor placed on the external surface of the capacitors. Electrical PD measurements, while possible in well controlled laboratory conditions, can not be practical on site. The main task of this paper is to verify the efficiency of the alternative acoustical measurements, which may be more easily applied in the field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnosis and recognition of partial discharges sources with a PD analysing system in a production high voltage test lab
abstract: Phase resolved PD distributions and the evolution of the PD values during the measuring time which are perceived by trained operators were up to now described by hand made pictures, with some comments and appreciations. In recent time, PD recording and analysing systems are available on the market. This paper reports on the practical use of a PD analysing system TEAS 570 in connection with a research and development order on a 110 kV oil impregnated voltage transformer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of the ratio of the PD damaging energy to the measurable input energy for a PD afflicted solid insulation
abstract: In practice, there is no available general relationship between the measurable transferred energy into the insulation of a test object and the damaging energy inside the partial discharge (PD) afflicted void. One of the reasons is that there is no applicable general model from which such a relationship can be concluded. This paper sheds light on a new method for determining generally the required energy relationship based on a mathematical model for a modified extended equivalent circuit of a PD afflicted solid insulation. The relationship can be obtained from a simulated PD signal. For simplicity and clarity a solid insulation bulk with only one void which has one PD source is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharges in flat, dielectric/metallic bounded cavities
abstract: Investigations were made on the character of partial discharges (PDs) in a flat, circular, airfilled cavity (height O.1 mm) with one dielectric and one metallic end-face. High frequency detection of PDs in the metal/dielectric cavity showed very characteristic pulse shapes, which partly could be related to discharge sequences inside the cavity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge characteristics in SF/sub 6//gas mixtures with the influence of N/sub 2/
abstract: This paper describes the partial discharge characteristics of SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ and SF/sub 6//gas+N/sub 2/ mixtures. In the latter mixtures 1% of triethylamine, trichlorotrifluoroethane (R113), tetrachloroethylene, perfluorocarbons and N/sub 2/ with SF/sub 6/ gas is implemented. The addition of N/sub 2/ gas to these mixtures show different measurements of partial discharge level. The N/sub 2/ synergism in the gas mixtures is also discussed. These experimental investigations era carried out in a non-uniform field under an a.c. applied voltage condition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of barriers on the penetration of solid insulation by discharges
abstract: This work investigates possible correlations between electrical discharge tree growth and the mechanical characteristics and strain associated with additives in resin based composite insulation. It is shown that the resistance presented by a barrier to tree growth is determined by fracture toughness, thermal resistance and work of adhesion. A high work of adhesion prevents interfacial tracking but, as importantly, leads to internal strain which, if compressive, substantially enhances tree resistance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge detection in high voltage rotating machines
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) measurement of turbine generators under operating condition is disturbed by noise originating from arcing, sparking and corona outside generators. Characteristics of both the external noise and PD in stator windings are investigated by using simultaneous measurement with multiple sensors located inside and outside an operating turbine generator. Pulses of the external noise detected with capacitive couplers inside the generator do not have high frequency components as the PD pulses have. The pulses occurring at a grounding brush of the rotor shaft propagate into the stator windings and are detected with the capacitive couplers. The radiation from unknown noise sources outside the generator induces pulses in PD detection circuits. The external noise from isolated phase bus and exciter slip rings was not found with the capacitive couplers in this experiment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new PD calibration technique based on the transfer function of stator windings
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) calibration for PD detection in electrical machines must be done to obtain accurate and reliable measurement results. However, difficulties in PD calibration exist in that results from different machines cannot be compared on the basis of PD readings and different detectors applied to the same winding will generally produce different values of PD magnitude. This is due to the fact that the propagation of the discharge pulse from the discharge site to the detector is extremely complex owing to a series of factors, including attenuation, reflection, resonance, radiation, impedance mismatch, grounding, etc., which affect the PD test results. This problem is compounded by the variety of detectors in use with variable bandwidth, centre frequency, cut-off frequencies, amplification coefficients and input impedance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Peak structure in PD spectra of hydrogenerators through "HF grounding" of the couplers and "time and amplitude" calibration
abstract: In order to develop a reliable tool for the maintenance planning of hydrogenerators, research works have been pursued to improve the immunity to noise of the "differential" technique of partial discharge measurements (PD). In this paper is presented 1) the "high-frequency grounding" technique that has been developed at IREQ to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of PD measurements systems and 2) the "time and amplitude" calibration technique that has been concurrently developed to achieve the low noise levels required for PD spectra measurements. Following the implementation on hydrogenerators of the HF grounding technique and of the enhanced calibration technique, noise-free PD spectra have been obtained. It is believed that these noise-free spectra will be more sensitive for the monitoring of the insulation conditions with time and for the detection of insulation defects at their early stages of development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of streamer propagation in dielectric liquids by using the finite element method
abstract: Prebreakdown phenomena in n-hexane and cyclohexane are studied numerically by using the two-dimensional finite element method (FEM). In this study, the streamer propagation is considered as a generation of a gas bubble in the liquid. The model of a point-plane geometry (non-uniform field) is presented to simulate the streamer growth and the positive and negative streamer velocities are calculated. The obtained results shoved a good agreement with the published experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of light emission techniques to study the spatial and temporal development of partial discharge activity during initiation and growth of electrical trees
abstract: Electrical treeing is the main long term failure process in synthetic resin insulators. Void formation at a region of local electrical stress enhancement (tree initiation), is followed by the growth of fine erosion channels (tree growth stage) driven by partial discharge (PD) activity. In this paper we report on ultra-sensitive non-evasive light detection techniques (using a photomultiplier and liquid nitrogen and Peltier cooled charge coupled device (CCD) cameras) which we have used to study i) the tree initiation processes which lead to PD and ii) the spatial and temporal development of PD activity and its relationship to damage accumulation during tree growth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Separation of partial discharges from pulse shaped noise signals with the help of neural networks
abstract: The paper introduces a method to separate Partial Discharges (PD) from pulse shaped noise signals using a neural network. After a short introduction of the applied neural network, its ability to classify PD and pulse shaped noise is demonstrated on simulated PD and noise pulses. Furthermore, with the help of signals injected at different points of a transformer coil, the possibilities and limits of the neural network used for a distinction of pulses is shown. The paper ends with a presentation of the first results of the neural network in the classification of signals measured on a power transformer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detection and localisation of internal defects in insulating system of power transformers
abstract: With the development of both fast and low cost analog to digital converters (ADC) and new mathematical procedures for waveform description, such as "Time Encoded Signal Processing And Recording" (TESPAR), new possibilities to detect and localize internal defects in insulating systems of power transformers become feasible if the following requirements are fulfilled: (1) the equivalent circuit of the insulating system for fast partial discharge (PD) signal propagation (ns time range) is known, (2) the measured response of the insulating system to the PD signal injected at least at three different positions of each winding (top, center, bottom) are calculated or measured at the signal tap-off points (i.e. bushings) and (3) the pattern matrix of all calculated or measured responses exist (encoded and processed signals with TESPAR) as a reference. In this contribution the above mentioned requirements for quasi simultaneous detection and localization of internal defects in insulating systems of power transformers is discussed. The application of this method for PD-measurements of real power transformers is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mechanism of degradation of polymers under corona streamers: relative humidity influence
abstract: In this article we study of the degradation induced by streamers on the surface of a polypropylene film, from the chemical point of view as well as the morphological, by changing the relative humidity in the air in which the discharge develops. We show certain degradation kinetics of polypropylene undergoing partial discharges in air depend closely on the relative humidity. There exists a critical energy for nodule formation, starting from the creation of oligomers by the discharge, and a critical time beyond which the nodules are transformed into the form of crystals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of partial discharge by applying rectangular pulse voltage
abstract: We measured the partial discharge (PD) characteristics by means of a bridge circuit when a rectangular pulse voltage or an ac voltage is applied. The qmax for the rectangular pulse voltage increased with the applied voltage, however, the qmax for the ac voltage did not depend on the applied voltage. We believe it is affected by the delay time of the PD occurrence. We also measured the PD characteristics when the width of the rectangular pulse voltage was changed. At a range shorter than 10 mu s, we found one PD at the pulse top and a few small PDs or no PDs after the trailing part. We consider that the interval time between the PDs that occur at the pulse top and after the trailing part will affect the PD characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
